newsitem.title: USA: Clinton starts week of rest on golf course.
newsitem.headline: Clinton starts week of rest on golf course.

text.p: President Bill Clinton flew to South Carolina on Monday to begin a week-long vacation, going directly from the airport to a golf course to play a round with Indiana Gov. Evan Bayh.

Accompanied by his wife Hillary and their daughter Chelsea, Clinton planned to usher in the New Year at Renaissance Weekend, an annual invitation-only gathering the first family has attended for years, long before they came to Washington.
The several hundred participants and their families represent a cross-section of backgrounds -- ranging from politicians and business leaders to artists and members of the news media.

Clinton plunged into the spirit of the annual get-together, which mixes discussion group chats with recreational activities, by going directly to George Fazio Golf Course and a round of golf with the Indiana governor and his wife Susan.

Clinton was laughing and telling stories as the group began their game. After playful chatter that a "presidential pardon" would be appropriate if the first shot was errant, Clinton's first swing sent his golf ball straight down the fairway.

Indiana's first lady, however, shanked her ball as reporters, photographers and a television camera crew recorded the moment. "One more, Susan," Clinton decreed. Her second shot was better, and the group hurried off to leave the news media behind.
Clinton on Monday night was expected to attend a private dinner honouring retired Admiral Elmo Zumwalt, who commanded U.S. naval forces during the Vietnam War.
The Clintons plan to depart South Carolina on New Year's Day for the U.S. Virgin Islands, where they plan to relax before returning to Washington Sunday.
